questions.q: Why are enterprise structure decisions made earlier than individual module configuration workbooks?
options: Because Oracle requires them to be configured alphabetically
Because they have no impact on reporting
Because almost every other setup object is scoped by a legal entity, business unit, or ledger, and changing them later is expensive
Because they are the least important decisions on the project
questions.explain: Enterprise structure decisions carry the largest blast radius since nearly every other setup object depends on them, making late changes costly.

questions.q: What does the "4 Cs" refer to in defining a ledger?
options: Cash, Credit, Currency, Control
Chart of accounts, Calendar, Currency, Convention
Configuration, Customization, Change, Compliance
Company, Country, Contract, Customer
questions.explain: A ledger is defined by its chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting convention (subledger accounting method) — the 4 Cs.

questions.q: What does a reference data set determine?
options: Whether reference data like payment terms is shared across business units or kept separate
The number of bank accounts a legal entity can have
The severity level of a Service Request
Whether UAT has passed
questions.explain: A reference data set groups reference data that can be shared across business units or kept separate, balancing standardization against unit-specific flexibility.

questions.q: Who typically reviews and approves enterprise structure design decisions, given their scope of impact?
options: Only the Functional Consultant for one module
Only Oracle Support
Only the Testing Lead
Finance leadership across every affected ledger and legal entity, sometimes including an auditor
questions.explain: Because the chart of accounts and ledger structure shape future financial statements, finance leadership across affected entities (sometimes with an auditor) reviews these decisions.

questions.q: What enterprise structure did Brightfield Industrial Group settle on?
options: Two legal entities, four business units, two ledgers
One US legal entity, two business units sharing one ledger, and one shared reference data set
No legal entities defined yet
A separate ledger for every business unit
questions.explain: Brightfield decided on one US legal entity, two business units (AP/Procurement and AR/Order Management) sharing a single ledger, and one shared reference data set.
